claim: *The behavioral move: states and transitions.* A model keeps the legal states and the permitted transitions and discards the code; the transition it omits — here the skip from IDLE straight to DONE — is the behavior it forbids. Its analyses search for a reachable bad state or a required event that never arrives.

topology.description: Implementation reduced to legal state transitions; IDLE→DONE directly forbidden.

required_terms: Node = legal state; edge = permitted transition; path = admitted execution. Analyze reachability, safety and liveness.
bw_encoding: Black outlines and arrows; white nodes; sparse 3–7% gray groups. Every non-solid relation is locally labeled; no distinction depends on color.
redesign: Native semantic redraw; colors replaced by labeled relations and line conventions.
alt: An implementation reduces to a state model. IDLE starts RUNNING, which finishes at DONE or fails at FAILED. A crossed dashed arrow marks the forbidden direct IDLE-to-DONE transition. Labels distinguish the question, transition semantics and typical analyses. The candidate uses black lines, white backgrounds and sparse gray; meaning does not depend on color.
